name: Médoc

limits: For white wine, Alvarinho, Floréal, Liliorila and Sauvignac together: at most 5%
For red wine, Arinarnoa, Castets and Touriga Nacional together: at most 5%

climate.koppen_name: Temperate, no dry season, warm summer

keyfacts: Médoc AOC covers the northern third of the Médoc peninsula on the Left Bank of the Gironde estuary, and is the area once called Bas-Médoc.
Soils are Garonne gravel, Pyrenees gravel and clayey limestone, and heavy clay-rich areas suit Merlot better than Cabernet Sauvignon.
Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot are the main grapes, with Petit Verdot, Malbec, Cabernet Franc and Carmenère also allowed.
It is mostly an area of cooperatives, and none of its estates were included in the 1855 Bordeaux classification.

blurb.text: A Left Bank Bordeaux appellation on the northern Médoc peninsula, sometimes called Bas-Médoc. It makes almost only red wine, from Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Cabernet Franc and others.
